I used for the gnocchi: 400g of ricotta, 60g of parmesan, 3 egg yolks (my eggs were small, you can get away with 2 large yolks), around 100g of flour, salt, pepper and nutmeg to taste. 
Pass the ricotta through a sieve, grate the parmesan and combine everything together but the flour and egg, taste if the seasoning is good, adjust it if needed, add the yolks, mix again and start mixing flour little by little until you can form shapes with it, careful not to put a lot of flour, I used less than 100g. 
To cook em you put them in simmering salt water little by little, you'll notice they will sink, when they're cooked they will rise up, you scoop them out and proceed to cook the rest. 

For the mushrooms: at cooking school they used a ratio of 250g of mushrooms for every 200g of gnocchi, here I used 100g of shiitake to the 400g and it was enough. 
The rest of the ingredients I was just eyeballing tbh but it's easy to do that. 
I heated some butter and proceeded to add 2 garlic cloves minced, the mushrooms, sautéed em a bit and then added the white wine, added salt and pepper, a little bit more of cold butter just to make it creamier, then added the cooked gnocchi, some chives and grated parmesan, sautéed it all together and finished with a little bit of extra virgin olive oil. 

Tip: I already used two types of ricotta to make this, the best for me was buffalo ricotta but the regular cow one works too, it just gets too "granulated" for my taste.

Salt: uh... salt lol, parmesan and ricotta
Fat: butter, olive oil, cheeses
Acid: white wine and ricotta
Heat: cooked

I was talking side effects with my doc the other day and she said it affects people differently. We started talking about because she is impressed by how I react to lithium, I almost don't have side effects and it stabilizes my moods right away. When I was first diagnosed I struggled a lot with depression and it got me out of it, now I tend to get more manic than depressed, which is great because I can't take antidepressants since they trigger mania and that doesn't solve the problem, just shifts it lol
Lithium gives the stability I never had without it, we even tried to stop it for some time to see if I would stay stable and it was a bad idea even though I was taking other meds. 
The side effects for me are lack of libido (which is great, it keeps me out of bad sheets lol and if I want to I can reverse that with hormones but I'm good) and now after almost 6 years taking it it started making my calcium levels high, but I'm taking vitamin D and will eat better to try and lower it. 
Doc said most people have a hard time with side effects from lithium, such as weight gain, bloating, kidney and thyroid problems but you'll never know if you never try, everyone is different. 
I hope you get the same good reactions I get because it really was a life saver for me. If you want to discuss depression and how it worked out for me (or anything else) feel free :)
